# Full vision-tower numerical counterexample and rebuilt integration

V116 ordinary integrated correctness passes all 167 assertions against its complete source archive. The following V117 build adds only a diagnostic for the trained vision tower at 256/512/1024/1536 pixel squares, with a red field and one blue quadrant. All repeated padded outputs are byte-identical and finite. Maximum-grid padded tower peak is 2011580048 bytes; the 1024-pixel original/candidate comparison peaks at 2532984344 bytes. These bounded correctness-run samples do not qualify serving footprint or latency.

Two of 19 declared assertions fail: padded-128 versus original BF16 whole-tower cosine is 0.9978315219027164 at 512 pixels and 0.9972843675032463 at 1024, below the prospectively declared 0.998 threshold. Worst-token cosines are reported, not silently thresholded. This numerical counterexample is preserved, despite component Float64 checks passing. Padding stays off; the frozen image-serving studies are not launched pending numerical resolution. No tolerance is loosened. A separate independent Float32/dtype-band investigation can determine whether the discrepancy is candidate error, reference rounding or both; no such oracle result exists yet. Maximum-grid assertions cover determinism/finiteness/resource bounds, not an independent complete-tower oracle.

Earlier independent dtype-band results on other images remain valid in their original scope. They do not certify these new fixtures.
